messages.subject: SWAT+ Parameter calibration or optimization using R-SWAT
messages.subject_clean: SWAT+ Parameter calibration or optimization using R-SWAT
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I am a beginner for SWAT+ and R-SWAT.

In R-SWAT, SWAT+ parameter sampling was done as the 2nd step, Run SWAT was done as the 3rd step and Evaluate Output was done as the 4th step.

Only in the 4th step we have to select the Observed Data file (ie after running the R-SWAT).

My question is ,
Parameter calibration is a process of adjusting model parameter values within their plausible ranges to minimize the differences between simulated and observed values.
If we select  the Observed Data file (4th step) after running RSWAT (3rd step), how the above could be achieved by the R-SWAT?

Look forward to hearing from you.

Thank you
Thushara

messages.subject: Re: New features were added to SWATshiny: DDS optimization, Sobol for sensitivity analysis, visualization
messages.subject_clean: New features were added to SWATshiny: DDS optimization, Sobol for sensitivity analysis, visualization
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sir,
I used DDS approach for my calibration for 500 iterations with parallel approach 2. The "currentsimulationreport" shows 594 rows implying 594 iterations if I am not wrong. Normally when I used Sensi_cali Hypercube sampling, it took only 5 days to simulated the same input. Does it take more time for DDS?

I look forward to your answer.

Kind Regards,
Divya

On Tuesday, September 7, 2021 at 9:44:10 PM UTC+2 Tam Nguyen wrote:
> A visual description of different parallel approach used for DDS
>
> On Tuesday, September 7, 2021 at 9:42:01 PM UTC+2 Tam Nguyen wrote:
> > Dear all,
> >
> > I have added some new features to SWATshiny as follows:
> >
> > 1. Dynamically dimensioned search (DDS) algorithm for parameter optimization: This can be run in parallel in different ways:
> >
> > Parallel approach 1: DDS is run independently on each core
> > Parallel approach 2:  DDS run on n cores and the best parameter from n cores at ith iteration is used as an initial parameter set for all cores in the next iteration. (suggested reading:  https://doi.org/10.1029/2005WR004723)
> > If you just want to use a normal approach, set number of core to 1, then parallel approaches 1 and 2 are identical and is exactly the one described in the aforementioned paper
> >
> > 2. Sobol for global parameter sensitivity analysis (more detail please see the sensitivity package: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sensitivity/index.html
> >
> > 3. Visualization of watout.dat file type (can be done independently from model calibration/parameter sensitivity - that why it is not numbered, e.g., 6. Visualization)
> >
> > Cheers,
> > Tam
> >
> >
> >

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have used DSS with parallel approach 2 for calibrating the runoff with 500 iteration. In the "currentsimulationreport",there are already 594 rows. Doesnot this mean that the iteration area done 594 times? If so, Why is RSWAT still running? I tried to check if there are any outputs in any of the CORES. There are no outputs in any of the 6 cores that I am using. With UNIFORM LAITN HYPERCUBE SAMPLING, it took 5 days o complete the simulation with same sets of input. Its been 6 days since the model has been running with DDS approach. Do you have any idea what might be the issue?

I look forward to an answer.

Kind Regards,
Divya Bhandary
